### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.files

### Description

I don't know if it is actually true, but i have the impression that using `vim.o.autochdir = true` conflicts with `mini.files` to some extend.

My observations after a lot of trial and error:

- I like to hop between directories a lot and often i open the explorer, enter `:cd /tmp` while the explorer is open and expect to update the view.
- I sometimes do `go_in_plus` close/reopen the explorer (`.open()`) and i am left with a "rogue floating window", apparently without `minifiles` filetype mappings. i can usually close those "zombies" with `:q` though. My guess is that after creating the buffer for the file i just opened move the cwd and closing/opening the explorer somehow creates a zombie float.

So i wonder: Is autochdir generally a problematic setting to have togehter with mini.files or is it just a configuration issue. For example it tried to make it work with:

```lua
-- refresh mini.files explorer when current cwd changes
-- e.g. by `:cd /path/to/different/dir`
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("DirChanged", {
  pattern = "*",
  callback = function()
    if MiniFiles.get_explorer_state() then -- check if we have an open explorer
      MiniFiles.open(vim.fn.getcwd()) -- re-open for changed cwd
    end
  end,
})
```

inside the `require("mini.files").setup()` block.

> * I like to hop between directories a lot and often i open the explorer, enter `:cd /tmp` while the explorer is open and expect to update the view.

I don't think this is a good workflow to support out of the box. Mostly because there is no significant obstacles to doing `:cd` *before* opening explorer. There is also [an example](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/d7ba1dec0082b7a542aa79c327e9554d4a27cc2c/doc/mini-files.txt#L510-L515) for custom mapping to set Neovim's current directory to the currently viewed directory in explorer.

> * I sometimes do `go_in_plus` close/reopen the explorer (`.open()`) and i am left with a "rogue floating window", apparently without `minifiles` filetype mappings. i can usually close those "zombies" with `:q` though. My guess is that after creating the buffer for the file i just opened move the cwd and closing/opening the explorer somehow creates a zombie float.

I also have no reasonable idea why this might have fixed the issue.

It is also not quite clear what *exactly* have you changed: did you add the `vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("User", {` call inside 'DirChanged' event callback with the same content as the first code block? If yes, then I'd might warn you that this will create a *new* autocommand each time you do the `:cd` when explorer is open (after doing this couple of times, executing `:au User` will show multiple `MiniFilesBufferCreate` autocommands), which is not great. The proper ways around this is to use `:h augroup` / `:h nvim_create_augroup()` or cache the created autocommand identifier (output of `:h nvim_create_autocmd()`) while making sure that it is removed before the next similar autocomman creation.

If some manipulation with nested autocommand creation has helped here, there is also a chance that the outer `DirChanged` command needs `nested = true` (`:h autocmd-nested`) flag to fix the initial case.

Do you literally have `local foo = event.data and event.data.foo or "a value"` as a body of the callback and this seems to fix the issue? If both are a "yes", then this is either a *very* weird issue or it doesn't really fix anything.

Also, I'd highly suggest merging all autocommands for 'MiniFilesBufferCreate' into a single autocommand. There is no good reason for keeping them separate while executing many different autocommands affects performance.

I think the body of the callback is more a spaghetticode debugging artifact. I think it should be enough to have the `vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd()` call in the `DirChanged` autocmd is what made it work. I'll follow your suggestion and streamline the config (removing the superfluous code and merging the autocmd's)
